books.section: Topic 6.6 The Rise of Industrial Capitalism
Industrialization, Corporate Consolidation, and the Gospel of Wealth

options.misconception: Background: Bell patented the telephone in 1876; Rockefeller worked in oil.
Background: Drake drilled the first oil well in 1859; Rockefeller entered the business by refining.
options.text: Because Rockefeller discovered oil in Pennsylvania
Because he organized business, not by inventing machines

options.misconception: Background: wealthy Americans existed long before Rockefeller; his fame is about organization at a new scale.
options.text: Because Rockefeller was the first American to become rich

rationales.A: Background: the telephone belongs to Bell and to the chapter on invention. Rockefeller’s story is oil and organization.
rationales.B: Background: Drake drilled the first well in 1859. Rockefeller built his power by refining and combining, not by discovery.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Rockefeller’s mark was the trust, horizontal integration, and control of an industry — new ways of organizing business, not a new invention.
rationales.D: Background: America had rich men before the Civil War. Rockefeller stands out for the scale and organization of his company.
rationales.general:
Ask what the man is famous for.
1. The portrait shows Rockefeller, but he invented no famous machine.
2. Background from the books: his fame rests on the trust and on buying out rival refiners.
3. Those are ways of organizing business, and they changed how whole industries worked.
4. That is why he belongs with the capitalists, not the inventors.
Remember: sort a figure by what changed because of him, not by his dates.
